hook: 214 people trapped at a lake, wildfire on every side.
narration: Two hundred fourteen people were trapped at a mountain lake, with a wildfire closing in on every side.
It was the Creek Fire in California, and nobody knew they were there.
Overhead, an Air Force drone crew from Ohio was scanning through the smoke with an infrared camera.
On a lake inside the fire, the sensor operator spotted dots. He zoomed in. Cars. He zoomed in again. People.
Infrared reads heat, so the camera sees the ground through smoke that blinds a pilot.
The first rescue flight was called off. That night, Army helicopters went in anyway, almost blind in the smoke.
There were more people than anyone expected. [short pause] The ones left for the next trip were told to jump in the lake if the fire got too close.
outcome: In three trips each, two helicopters flew out all two hundred fourteen people.
title: 214 people trapped by a wildfire
description:
During California's Creek Fire in 2020, an Ohio Air National Guard MQ-9 sensor operator spotted 214 people trapped at a lake inside the fire, and Army helicopters flew them out in three trips each.

Footage: U.S. Air National Guard video by Staff Sgt. Zachary Tateman, 178th Wing, via DVIDS: https://www.dvidshub.net/video/780524/sensor-operator-saves-lives-during-california-wildfires
